title: Pokémon Red
features: The revolutionary beginning: catching and trading 151 monsters
Link Cable support for head-to-head multiplayer battles
Non-linear Kanto gym challenge across 8 elemental badges
Turn-based RPG battle system with elemental type match-ups
Legendary birds and the elusive Mythical Pokémon Mew

villainTeam.name: Team Rocket
villainTeam.goal: Exploiting Pokémon for monetary profit and world domination

trivia: Satoshi Tajiri conceived Pokémon inspired by his childhood insect collecting hobby.
Mew was secretly programmed into the game cartridge by Shigeki Morimoto just weeks before release.
Psychic-type had virtually no weaknesses in Gen 1 due to a coding glitch making Ghost-type ineffective.
overview: Hello there! Welcome to the world of Pokémon! Pokémon Red sparked a worldwide cultural phenomenon, placing Pallet Town's young trainer on an unforgettable journey to conquer the Indigo Plateau and record every creature in the Pokédex!

title: Pokémon Green
features: Original Japanese launch title paired with Pocket Monsters Red
Historical early sprite artwork by Ken Sugimori and Atsuko Nishida
Exclusive encounter tables differing from the later international Blue
Birth of the iconic Cerulean Cave and MissingNo. glitch encounters
Groundwork for Game Freak's innovative creature trading economy

villainTeam.name: Team Rocket
villainTeam.goal: Kidnapping rare species to fund an underground criminal empire

trivia: Never officially released in English outside Japan; international versions were built on the revised Blue engine.
Green features charmingly bizarre early sprite designs that were later polished for global release.
Its mascot Venusaur represents the lush flora flourishing across the unspoiled Kanto countryside.
overview: Ah, the original Japanese masterpiece that initiated it all! Pokémon Green captures the raw, unfiltered passion of Game Freak's earliest ambitions, introducing trainers to the tranquil greenery of Kanto.

title: Pokémon Blue
features: Overhauled graphics, cleaned audio registers, and patched map bugs
Mascot Blastoise leading the charge on international cartridge art
Rebalanced wild encounter tables designed for cooperative trading
Indigo Plateau gauntlet with climatic rival showdown
The definitive Gen 1 blueprint used to localize Red and Blue worldwide

villainTeam.name: Team Rocket
villainTeam.goal: Stealing valuable Pokémon and seizing the Silph Co. Master Ball

trivia: Originally a mail-order exclusive for CoroCoro Comic readers in Japan before hitting retail stores.
The North American release combined Japanese Blue's engine with Japanese Red and Green's version-exclusive Pokémon distribution.
Blastoise's dual water cannons made it an instant icon on playgrounds worldwide.
overview: Behold, the cool blue waters of competitive spirit! Pokémon Blue introduced refined sprites and legendary encounters, serving as the trusted international companion to Red throughout Pokémania's zenith!

title: Pokémon Yellow: Special Pikachu Edition
features: Walking Pokémon mechanic: Pikachu happily follows behind your avatar
Pikachu mood meter with voiced sound clips recorded by Ikue Otani
Anime-inspired narrative featuring Jessie, James, and Meowth encounters
Opportunity to obtain all three traditional Kanto starters in a single playthrough
Surfing Pikachu minigame playable when transferring a special event Pikachu

villainTeam.name: Team Rocket
villainTeam.goal: Stealing rare specimens alongside the bungling duo Jessie and James

trivia: Pikachu refuses to evolve into Raichu via Thunder Stone, directly mirroring Ash Ketchum's partner in the anime.
The starter Pikachu possesses an animated face dialogue box that displays various emotional reactions.
Your rival's Eevee evolves into Jolteon, Flareon, or Vaporeon depending on early-game battle outcomes.
overview: Remarkable! What a bond between Trainer and partner! Pokémon Yellow brought the beloved animated television series straight into your hands, letting every child adventure shoulder-to-shoulder with Pikachu!

title: Pokémon Gold
features: 100 new species expanding the National Pokédex to 251 entries
Real-time internal clock powering day/night cycles and weekly events
Pokémon breeding, Daycare mechanics, and introduction of Baby Pokémon
Steel and Dark types introduced to tame the overpowering Psychic meta
Entire Kanto region unlocked after beating the Elite Four for 16 total badges

villainTeam.name: Team Rocket
villainTeam.goal: Hijacking the Goldenrod Radio Tower to broadcast a summons to Giovanni

trivia: Satoru Iwata compressed the game's code so efficiently that Game Freak was able to fit all of Kanto on the cartridge.
The climactic battle against Pokémon Trainer Red atop Mt. Silver remains one of gaming's greatest boss fights.
Introduced Shiny Pokémon, with the Red Gyarados at Lake of Rage as a guaranteed encounter.
overview: Astounding scientific progress! Pokémon Gold expanded our horizons beyond Kanto into traditional Johto, gifting us with the mystery of Pokémon Eggs, real-world temporal cycles, and the resplendent rainbow wings of Ho-Oh!

title: Pokémon Silver
features: Deep-sea guardian Lugia resting in the Whirl Islands abyss
Held items mechanic allowing strategic passive combat benefits
Pokégear device featuring mobile phone calls, map card, and radio tuner
Special stat split into Special Attack and Special Defense attributes
Roaming Legendary Beasts: Entei, Raikou, and Suicune across Johto roads

villainTeam.name: Team Rocket
villainTeam.goal: Restoring the glory of Team Rocket and severing Slowpoke tails for illicit cash

trivia: Lugia was originally created specifically for the second movie (The Power of One) by writer Takeshi Shudo before being adopted into the games.
The Silver Wing key item was required to access the deepest sanctuary of the Whirl Islands.
Karen of the Elite Four delivered the legendary quote about winning with your favorites rather than strong or weak Pokémon.
overview: Listen closely to the tides! Pokémon Silver unveiled the enigmatic guardian of the seas, Lugia! Between breeding newfound species and challenging two complete continents, it stands as an enduring monument of adventure!

title: Pokémon Crystal
features: Historic choice to select a female protagonist (Kris) for the first time
Animated battle sprites greeting players at the start of every encounter
Battle Tower introduction: an endless endgame competitive trial
Expanded lore regarding Suicune and the enigmatic seeker Eusine
Mobile Adapter GB integration in Japan allowing remote mobile trading

villainTeam.name: Team Rocket
villainTeam.goal: Desperately trying to re-establish Team Rocket's hierarchy from Mahogany Town

trivia: The first Pokémon cartridge made exclusively for the Game Boy Color, unable to run on the original monochrome Game Boy.
The Japanese version allowed players to obtain the mythical Celebi via the Mobile Adapter GB.
Kris's design set the standard for female protagonist options in all subsequent mainline titles.
overview: Pure elegance crystallized in time! Pokémon Crystal brought motion to Pokémon sprites and welcomed young women into the role of Pokémon Champions, pursuing the north wind incarnate, Suicune!

title: Pokémon Ruby
features: Invention of Pokémon Abilities and 25 distinct Natures
Double Battles introducing cooperative team synergy
Pokémon Contests scoring Cool, Beauty, Cute, Smart, and Tough moves
Secret Bases customizable with decorations and mats across trees and caves
Dynamic weather states including drought, downpours, and sandstorms

villainTeam.name: Team Magma
villainTeam.goal: Awakening Groudon to evaporate the oceans and expand terrestrial landmass

trivia: Norman is the first and only in-game biological father of the player character to serve as a Gym Leader.
Gen 3 completely rebuilt the internal data structure for Pokémon (IVs, EVs, PID), severing backward compatibility with Gen 1 and 2.
The Braille puzzles required to unlock the Legendary Titans (Regirock, Regice, Registeel) delighted codebreakers.
overview: What radiant sunshine! Welcome to tropical Hoenn! Pokémon Ruby revolutionized competitive strategy with innate Abilities and Natures, while pitting trainers against the blazing terrestrial fury of ancient Groudon!

title: Pokémon Sapphire
features: Underwater diving mechanics exploring trench beds and deep oceanic rifts
Eco-focused narrative confronting the oceanic expansionists of Team Aqua
Pokéblock crafting and Berry Blending for Contest preparation
Introduction of Ribbon rewards commemorating champion feats
Expansive water routes teeming with diverse pelagic species

villainTeam.name: Team Aqua
villainTeam.goal: Awakening Kyogre to trigger torrential rains and expand the ocean realm

trivia: Kyogre's Drizzle ability permanently kept torrential rain active until another weather move or Pokémon canceled it.
Hoenn's soundtrack made prominent and beloved use of the GBA's synthetic brass instruments.
The Mach Bike and Acro Bike offered different physics and puzzle-solving tools for traversing mountains.
overview: Dive into the mysterious azure deep! Pokémon Sapphire submerged players into Hoenn's magnificent ocean trenches, confronting Team Aqua and calming the cataclysmic deluges of Kyogre!

title: Pokémon FireRed
features: Faithful, full-color remake of the inaugural Kanto journey on GBA hardware
Brand-new Sevii Islands archipelago introducing post-game Johto lore
Bundled with the Game Boy Advance Wireless Adapter for cordless trading
Help System and Fame Checker recording dialogue and lore tips
Teachy TV teaching novice trainers competitive battle fundamentals

villainTeam.name: Team Rocket
villainTeam.goal: Controlling the Kanto underworld and exploiting the Sevii Islands' Ruby and Sapphire gems

trivia: The Sevii Islands connected Kanto directly with Hoenn lore via the Ruby and Sapphire network machine.
Introduced female protagonist Leaf to the Kanto storyline for the very first time.
The Wireless Adapter let up to five players chat and trade in the Union Room without cables.
overview: Ah, Pallet Town! It warms my heart to see our humble beginnings rebuilt so vividly! Pokémon FireRed modernized Kanto with lush 32-bit visuals, Abilities, and the sprawling Sevii Islands!

title: Pokémon LeafGreen
features: Re-imagined retelling of the original Green version for international audiences
Wireless Union Room and Direct Corner multiplayer lobby features
National Dex quest unlocking Gen 2 species in the Sevii Islands
Remastered 8-bit classic soundtrack by Junichi Masuda and Go Ichinose
Vs. Seeker item allowing seamless rematches with outdoor trainers

villainTeam.name: Team Rocket
villainTeam.goal: Harvesting Pokémon power while hunting legendary birds across Kanto

trivia: Marks the first time western players officially experienced the 'Green' counterpart to Red in any format.
The Vs. Seeker battery charged dynamically as the player took 100 steps in the overworld.
Mewtwo's Cerulean Cave encounter required extensive Sevii Island gemstone quests to reopen.
overview: Nature flourishes in every pixel! Pokémon LeafGreen finally brought the spirit of Pocket Monsters Green across the seas, packaged with timeless Kanto gym battles and modern GBA mechanics!

title: Pokémon Emerald
features: Climactic dual-villain clash with Rayquaza descending from the ozone layer
Legendary Battle Frontier featuring 7 unique battle facilities and Frontier Brains
Animated battle sprites returned to the Game Boy Advance generation
Gym Leader rematches via the upgraded PokéNav Match Call feature
Breeding enhancements including Everstone nature passing and Flame Body hatching

villainTeam.name: Team Magma & Team Aqua
villainTeam.goal: Simultaneously triggering apocalypse through Groudon and Kyogre before Rayquaza intervenes

trivia: The Battle Frontier in Emerald set an unmatched gold standard for endgame challenge in the franchise.
Juan replaced Wallace as the Sootopolis Gym Leader, allowing Wallace to step up as the Hoenn Champion.
Rayquaza's cutscene stopping Groudon and Kyogre is widely considered one of the coolest pixel cutscenes in gaming.
overview: Behold the sky dragon's majestic descent! Pokémon Emerald united both terrestrial and marine legends under the awe-inspiring dominion of Rayquaza, capped off by the supreme challenge of the Battle Frontier!

title: Pokémon Diamond
features: The game-changing Physical / Special move split by individual move mechanics
Nintendo Wi-Fi Connection introducing global online battling and trading
Global Trade System (GTS) enabling worldwide trade listings
The Underground allowing fossil excavation and underground secret bases
Pokétch dual-screen utility wristband with 25 diverse applications

villainTeam.name: Team Galactic
villainTeam.goal: Capturing Dialga atop Spear Pillar to eradicate emotion and forge a universe devoid of spirit

trivia: The Physical/Special split finally allowed Pokémon like Gengar (Ghost/Poison) and Gyarados (Water/Flying) to use physical moves with high attack stats.
Cynthia's terrifying battle theme and diverse team spearheaded by Garchomp made her an enduring fan legend.
Flint of the Elite Four only had two actual Fire-types (Rapidash and Infernape) due to the limited Sinnoh regional dex.
overview: Time itself pulses with anticipation! Welcome to snowy Sinnoh! Pokémon Diamond opened up the dual screens of the Nintendo DS, fundamentally perfecting competitive combat through the legendary Physical/Special split!

title: Pokémon Pearl
features: Spatial deity Palkia dominating the celestial crest of Mt. Coronet
Touch-screen navigation for PC boxes, party management, and Pokétch
Super Contests featuring dress-up visual evaluation and rhythm dance stages
Ball Capsules allowing customizable battle entrance particle seals
Voice chat capability supported through the Nintendo DS built-in microphone

villainTeam.name: Team Galactic
villainTeam.goal: Summoning Palkia with the Red Chain to warp spatial dimensions to his nihilistic whim

trivia: Palkia's signature Spacial Rend move commands incredible critical hit ratios.
The GTS station in Jubilife City featured a giant spinning globe displaying trainer trade origins.
Sinnoh introduced gender differences in Pokémon sprites, such as female Pikachu having heart-shaped tails.
overview: Dimensions warp and weave around us! In Pokémon Pearl, trainers scale the majestic peaks of Mt. Coronet to defend the very fabric of space against Team Galactic's heartless ambitions!

title: Pokémon Platinum
features: The mind-bending Distortion World featuring gravity-defying physics
Expanded Sinnoh Pokédex to 210 species resolving Fire-type rarity
Brand-new Battle Frontier with the Battle Factory, Castle, and Arcade
Upgraded battle surf and engine speed resolving Diamond and Pearl sluggishness
Vs. Recorder saving competitive Wi-Fi battle replays for sharing

villainTeam.name: Team Galactic
villainTeam.goal: Vanishing into the antimatter Distortion World after awakening Giratina's primal fury

trivia: Giratina's Origin Forme is unlocked when holding the Griseous Orb or visiting the Distortion World.
Looker, the International Police detective, made his iconic debut in this title investigating Team Galactic.
The gym progression was tweaked, moving Fantina to the 3rd gym to prevent mid-game difficulty drops.
overview: Where gravity bends and shadows lengthen! Pokémon Platinum perfected the Sinnoh odyssey, transporting daring trainers into the antimatter abyss of the Distortion World alongside Renegade Giratina!

title: Pokémon HeartGold
features: Every single Pokémon capable of walking behind the player in the overworld
Bundled Pokéwalker pedometer accessory allowing real-world walking and catching
Pokéathlon minigames utilizing full touch-screen sports controls
GB Sounds key item swapping the entire DS soundtrack back to 8-bit chiptunes
All 16 Gym Badges across Johto and Kanto culminating in the Mt. Silver duel

villainTeam.name: Team Rocket
villainTeam.goal: Reassembling the executive cadre and seizing control of Goldenrod City

trivia: Widely celebrated among the community as the pinnacle of 2D Pokémon game design.
The Pokéwalker was tested by researchers and found to be one of the most accurate pedometers on the market.
Interacting with your following Pokémon reveals hundreds of unique contextual animations and emotional reactions.
overview: Heart and soul harmonized together! Pokémon HeartGold stands as an absolute love letter to the franchise, letting your dearest partner walk right behind you through two magnificent regions!

title: Pokémon SoulSilver
features: Breath-taking cinematic cutscene summoning Lugia behind the roaring waterfalls
Brand-new Johto Safari Zone customizable with dynamic terrestrial blocks
Battle Frontier imported directly from Platinum for premier endgame trials
Touch screen bottom menu interface allowing single-tap stylus management
Legendary Hoenn and Kanto encounters including Latias, Latios, and Groudon

villainTeam.name: Team Rocket
villainTeam.goal: Restoring Giovanni's reign and pillaging Slowpoke Well

trivia: Features a special in-game Celebi event revealing Silver's identity as Giovanni's estranged son.
The bottom screen remained persistently functional as a full menu interface without needing to pause the game.
Defeating Red unlocks Kanto starter gifts from Professor Oak and Hoenn starter gifts from Steven Stone.
overview: Listen to the song of the silver bell! Pokémon SoulSilver polished Johto's timeless heritage to mirror perfection, celebrating the bond between human and monster through every step of your journey!

title: Pokémon Black
features: 156 entirely new Pokémon: zero old species available until post-game credits
Deep thematic narrative exploring Pokémon liberation and moral philosophy
Fully animated battle sprites moving continuously during combat
Triple Battles and Rotation Battles introducing intense tactical options
Dynamic four-season system changing route maps every real-world month

villainTeam.name: Team Plasma
villainTeam.goal: Manipulating N to liberate all Pokémon so Ghetsis alone controls absolute power

trivia: First mainline region based outside Japan, drawing aesthetic inspiration from New York City.
The narrative breaks traditional convention: the Champion battle is interrupted as N's Castle erupts from the earth.
Features Black City, an exclusive urban post-game zone filled with high-level trainers.
overview: Truth and ideals clash in Unova! Pokémon Black dared to make trainers question the morality of catching Pokémon, introducing 156 brand-new creatures amidst a dramatic ideological confrontation!

title: Pokémon White
features: Pure unadulterated freshness: only Gen 5 Pokémon encounterable before Champion
White Forest: a tranquil natural preserve teeming with classic wild species
Musical Hall performances replacing traditional Pokémon Contests
Dynamic battle music shifting seamlessly when low on HP or facing a gym ace
C-Gear wireless hub linking Pass Power buffs and Entralink missions

villainTeam.name: Team Plasma
villainTeam.goal: Dividing Pokémon and humanity under the philosophical banner of King N

trivia: In White, young prodigy Iris serves as the 8th Gym Leader rather than the elder Drayden.
The Unova battle camera dynamically zoomed in and out during attacks, creating unparalleled visual kineticism on DS.
Zekrom's tail generator roars with lightning bolts to champion those fighting for pure ideals.
overview: Seek the ideals of the world! Pokémon White presented a thrilling, mature narrative that proved Pokémon could craft unforgettable story arcs, championed by the thunderous roar of Zekrom!

title: Pokémon Black 2
features: First direct mainline numbered narrative sequel set two years after B&W
Pokémon World Tournament (PWT) allowing battles against EVERY past Gym Leader and Champion
Pokéstar Studios: script-based Hollywood film mini-game with custom battles
Memory Link syncing save data from original Black/White for exclusive flashbacks
Challenge Mode & Easy Mode difficulty keys unlocking post-game adjustments

villainTeam.name: Neo Team Plasma
villainTeam.goal: Freezing Unova solid using the Plasma Frigate cannon powered by Kyurem

trivia: The Pokémon World Tournament is considered by many the finest celebratory battle facility in series history.
Features a 300-strong regional Pokédex mixing beloved old species with Gen 5 favorites right from Route 1.
The final mainline Pokémon release for the legendary Nintendo DS family.
overview: Two years later, Unova freezes over! Pokémon Black 2 delivered unmatched content volume, letting trainers compete in the grand Pokémon World Tournament alongside every historical Champion!

title: Pokémon White 2
features: Direct continuation tracking Hugh's vendetta to reclaim his sister's Purrloin
Fusion mechanic: DNA Splicers merging Kyurem with Reshiram into White Kyurem
Join Avenue: bustling commercial shopping street leveled up by player interactions
Habitat List tracking completed route capture logs inside the Pokédex
Medal Rally achievement system featuring 255 unique accomplishment medals

villainTeam.name: Neo Team Plasma
villainTeam.goal: Weaponizing Kyurem's chilling overdrive to bring Unova beneath their heel

trivia: White Treehollow provides a sprawling battle labyrinth ending in a shiny Gible or Dratini reward.
Iris ascending to the Champion throne with her celestial bedroom arena remains an unforgettable moment.
Colress's eccentric battle theme features an actual synthesized countdown timer.
overview: A triumphant finale to the sprite era! Pokémon White 2 packed the Nintendo DS to its absolute technological limits, pairing fusion mechanics with the pinnacle of 2D pixel battle art!

title: Pokémon X
features: Full leap into 3D polygonal models for all characters and over 700 Pokémon
Mega Evolution: temporary in-battle transcendent transformations
Introduction of Fairy-type: the first new elemental type in 14 years
Extensive Trainer Customization: clothes, haircuts, hats, and contact lenses
Player Search System (PSS) enabling instant peer-to-peer trading and Wonder Trade

villainTeam.name: Team Flare
villainTeam.goal: Firing the ancient Ultimate Weapon to exterminate life and preserve eternal beauty

trivia: The first mainline Pokémon games released simultaneously worldwide on the very same date.
Wonder Trade was invented here, introducing the thrilling mystery of blind international trades.
Xerneas represents the concept of eternal life, resting as a sacred dormant tree for millennia.
overview: Magnifique! Welcome to the fashion capital of Kalos! Pokémon X propelled our world into glorious three dimensions, unleashing the awe-inspiring spectacle of Mega Evolution!

title: Pokémon Y
features: The destruction avowed by Yveltal balancing Kalosian life and death lore
Pokémon-Amie: petting, feeding Poké Puffs, and bonding with your monsters
Super Training: minigames providing transparent access to Effort Values (EVs)
Sky Battles and Horde Encounters pitting single battlers against 5 wild foes
Roller skates and directional analog movement across Parisian boulevards

villainTeam.name: Team Flare
villainTeam.goal: Activating the Ultimate Weapon to purge the world of human greed

trivia: Fairy-type was specifically created to balance Dragon-type's competitive dominance since Gen 4.
Kalos was geographically inspired by France, with Lumiose City echoing Paris and its Eiffel Tower.
Yveltal's signature Oblivion Wing move drains immense HP from opponents into itself.
overview: Spread the wings of destruction! In Pokémon Y, the skies of Kalos darken with the omen of Yveltal, challenging brave trainers to master Fairy-types and wield Mega Evolution with honor!

title: Pokémon Omega Ruby
features: Primal Reversion unlocking prehistoric primordial titan powers
Soaring the Skies on Mega Latios / Latias in free-flight over Hoenn
DexNav sneaking mechanic tracking wild Pokémon with hidden abilities and egg moves
Delta Episode post-game quest journeying into outer space to shatter a meteor
Super-Secret Bases sharing customizable gyms via StreetPass and QR codes

villainTeam.name: Team Magma
villainTeam.goal: Restoring Groudon's Primal Reversion with the Red Orb to scorch the sea

trivia: Primal Groudon gains the Fire type and Desolate Land ability, which evaporates all incoming Water moves completely.
The Delta Episode introduces Zinnia and establishes the existence of alternate Pokémon multiverse timelines.
Mega Rayquaza is the only Pokémon able to Mega Evolve without holding a Mega Stone, requiring Dragon Ascent instead.
overview: Revisit Hoenn like never before! Pokémon Omega Ruby delivered breathtaking aerial freedom, allowing trainers to take to the skies and witness the apocalyptic grandeur of Primal Groudon!

title: Pokémon Alpha Sapphire
features: Primal Reversion awakening Kyogre's primordial Primordial Sea deluges
Mirage Spots hiding Legendary Pokémon spanning all past five generations
Cosplay Pikachu dressing up in unique competitive contest outfits
Revamped gym puzzles and lush 3D volcanic and oceanic biomes
Emotional musical score fully orchestrated with beloved brass arrangements

villainTeam.name: Team Aqua
villainTeam.goal: Restoring Kyogre to its primordial glory with the Blue Orb to flood the globe

trivia: Wally's final battle on Victory Road with his Gallade Mega Evolving to an epic rock theme is a franchise highpoint.
Primal Kyogre's Primordial Sea ability nullifies all Fire-type attacks from functioning.
The DexNav radar beeped louder as you crept closer to rare creatures lurking in the tall grass.
overview: The depths of the ocean call to us! Pokémon Alpha Sapphire reimagined Hoenn with staggering cinematic polish, inviting you to ride the torrential tides of Primal Kyogre across the Hoenn seas!

title: Pokémon Sun
features: Island Challenge replacing traditional Gyms with Totem Pokémon trials
Z-Moves: devastating once-per-battle ultimate powered kinetic strikes
Regional Variants: Alolan forms adapting Gen 1 classics to tropical climates
Removal of Hidden Machines (HMs) in favor of Ride Pokémon calling
Ultra Beasts: extraterrestrial entities originating from Ultra Space

villainTeam.name: Team Skull & Aether Foundation
villainTeam.goal: Lusamine opening Ultra Wormholes to commune with Nihilego at any cost

trivia: Released for the franchise's 20th anniversary celebration.
The player doesn't challenge an existing Champion; they establish the inaugural Alola Pokémon League as its first Champion.
Solgaleo is surprisingly Psychic/Steel despite being the sun emissary, referencing alchemy's devouring lion metaphor.
overview: Alola! Welcome to paradise! Pokémon Sun shattered twenty years of tradition by discarding HMs and Gyms for rich Island Trials, blessing us with radiant Solgaleo and tropical Alolan forms!

title: Pokémon Moon
features: 12-hour time shift: playing during day makes the game world nocturnal
Totem Pokémon calling SOS allies for intense tactical multi-target trials
Poké Pelago islands where boxed Pokémon harvest berries and train
Festival Plaza: multiplayer carnival for mini-missions and dye houses
Emotional character journey focused on Lillie and Nebby (Cosmog)

villainTeam.name: Team Skull & Aether Foundation
villainTeam.goal: Using Cosmog to unleash extraterrestrial Ultra Beasts into Alola

trivia: Because Moon is offset by 12 hours from the 3DS internal clock, nocturnal players experienced brilliant daytime sun.
Lunala transforms into its Full Moon phase when unleashing the terrifying Moongeist Beam attack.
Team Skull's rap gestures and hilarious self-awareness made Guzma an instant fan-favorite.
overview: Under the silver moonlight of Alola! Pokémon Moon touched the hearts of trainers through Lillie's brave journey with Nebby, soaring under the luminous celestial wings of Lunala!

title: Pokémon Ultra Sun
features: Climactic battle against Ultra Necrozma atop Megalo Tower
Ultra Warp Ride minigame steering through wormholes to alien worlds
Mantine Surf: trick-based oceanic transit linking Alola's islands
Episode RR confronting Team Rainbow Rocket featuring all past villain bosses
Battle Agency: renting competitive Pokémon for cooperative boss runs

villainTeam.name: Team Rainbow Rocket & Ultra Recon Squad
villainTeam.goal: Giovanni uniting villains from parallel dimensions to command an army of Ultra Beasts

trivia: Ultra Necrozma's boss fight is notorious for sweeping unprepared teams with its astronomical stat boosts.
The final mainline Pokémon release for the entire Nintendo 3DS family.
Features every single past legendary Pokémon in the Ultra Space Wilds.
overview: A darker shadow looms over paradise! Pokémon Ultra Sun challenged trainers with the blinding radiance of Ultra Necrozma and an unforgettable showdown against Team Rainbow Rocket!

title: Pokémon Ultra Moon
features: Dawn Wings fusion uniting Necrozma with Lunala to consume moonlight
Expanded Alola Pokédex welcoming Poipole, Naganadel, and Stakataka
Alola Photo Club capturing snapshots with your Pokémon with stickers and frames
Totem Stickers hidden across islands rewarding colossal Totem-sized Pokémon
Mina's new Fairy-type Island Trial resolving the unfinished Sun/Moon questline

villainTeam.name: Team Rainbow Rocket & Ultra Recon Squad
villainTeam.goal: Subjugating parallel realities using the combined might of Team Magma, Aqua, Galactic, Plasma, and Flare

trivia: Team Rainbow Rocket features alternate reality versions of villain leaders where they successfully achieved their evil plans.
Stakataka's design is based on a sentient stone fortress made of hundreds of individual eyes.
Molayne joined the Elite Four replacing Hala, specializing in defensive Steel-types.
overview: Traverse the Ultra Wormholes! Pokémon Ultra Moon concluded the handheld Nintendo 3DS legacy with deep dimensional lore, interdimensional villain reunions, and ultimate Z-Power!

title: Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu!
features: Overworld Pokémon spawns: eliminating random encounters completely
Motion-controlled catching mechanic inspired by Pokémon GO
Drop-in two-player local cooperative adventuring with a shared Joy-Con
Partner Pikachu riding on your shoulder with custom clothing and partner powers
Riding large Pokémon across water, land, and soaring over trees

villainTeam.name: Team Rocket
villainTeam.goal: Classic Kanto schemes alongside anime icons Jessie, James, and Meowth

trivia: First Pokémon mainline/core entry developed natively for high-definition television on Nintendo Switch.
Compatible with the Poké Ball Plus peripheral containing a real internal speaker and Mew gift.
Master Trainers populate the post-game, requiring 1-on-1 mirror matches with every single Kanto species.
overview: Pikachu, let's go! Bringing Kanto into vibrant high definition, this accessible entry united Pokémon GO players with mainline veterans, showing wild Pokémon freely roaming the grass for the first time!

title: Pokémon: Let's Go, Eevee!
features: Starter Eevee perching atop the player's cap with custom hairstyles
Exclusive Secret Techniques (Chop Down, Sea Skim) replacing all HM requirements
Partner Eevee learning unique elemental moves like Bouncy Bubble and Sizzly Slide
Seamless Pokémon GO connectivity via the GO Park in Fuchsia City
Meltan and Melmetal mythical integration debuting in the Pokémon world

villainTeam.name: Team Rocket
villainTeam.goal: Extorting Silph Co. and controlling the Lavender Town Pokémon Tower

trivia: Eevee's partner voice is performed by renowned voice actress Aoi Yuki.
Features cameos from classic series legends Red, Blue, and Green as elite post-game bosses.
The capture combo mechanic rewarded players with higher shiny odds and IVs for catching the same species repeatedly.
overview: Eevee's charming eyes shine bright! Pokémon: Let's Go, Eevee! made everyone's favorite evolution Pokémon the star of the show, proving that warmth, accessibility, and nostalgia make for pure magic!

title: Pokémon Sword
features: Dynamax and Gigantamax: colossal three-turn battlefield size transformations
The Wild Area: vast open-camera wilderness teeming with roaming giants
Four-player cooperative Max Raid Battles in glowing Pokémon Dens
Pokémon Camp: cooking curry recipes and playing with your party
Stadium sports atmosphere: roaring crowds chanting with dynamic battle themes

villainTeam.name: Team Yell & Macro Cosmos
villainTeam.goal: Awakening Eternatus to prevent a projected Galar energy crisis a millennium in the future

trivia: First mainline Pokémon games to receive post-launch Expansion Pass DLC instead of a third version.
The battle theme in Gym stadiums incorporates actual recorded soccer stadium crowd chanting.
Zacian's Intrepid Sword ability immediately boosts its Attack stat upon entering battle, making it a competitive powerhouse.
overview: Step onto the pitch as the crowd roars! Pokémon Sword turned Gym Battles into grand sporting spectacles in Galar, letting trainers supersize their favorites through the colossal spectacle of Dynamax!

title: Pokémon Shield
features: The steadfast shield wolf Zamazenta repelling the Darkest Day
Version-exclusive Gym Leaders Allister (Ghost) and Melony (Ice)
Max Lair cooperative Dynamax Adventures exploring legendary dens
Extensive Galarian regional evolutions including Obstagoon and Cursola
Y-Comm networking for online stamps, trading, and instant battle invites

villainTeam.name: Team Yell & Macro Cosmos
villainTeam.goal: Harvesting Galar particles from Eternatus beneath the Wyndon stadium

trivia: Piers is the first Gym Leader in Pokémon history who sings acapella and refuses to Dynamax his Pokémon.
The Crown Tundra DLC introduced Galarian forms of the legendary birds Articuno, Zapdos, and Moltres.
Leon's undefeated reputation and signature Charizard pose made him a central figure across the anime and games.
overview: Raise your shield against the storm! Pokémon Shield defended Galar with honor, offering cooperative Max Raid Battles in the Wild Area and heart-pounding stadium showdowns!

title: Pokémon Brilliant Diamond
features: Faithful top-down chibi art recreation of the original 2006 Sinnoh adventures
Grand Underground: massive subterranean network with elemental Pokémon Hideaways
Ramanas Park post-game sanctuary hosting past-generation Legendaries via slates
Modern quality-of-life: automatic EXP Share, autosave, and mobile box access
